property_summary: For any deployed C (reference), owner() always returns the address encoded in the first immutable arg slot (immutable arg offset 0x0); the mutant returns the second immutable arg instead, so for inputs where the first and second immutable args differ the mutant's owner() returns a different address and thus violates the property.

For every deployed correct C, owner() returns the address encoded at immutable arg slot 0 (the first immutable arg); the mutant reads slot 1 (second immutable arg) and so will return a different address when the first and second immutable args differ.

For any deployed correct C, owner() returns the address encoded in the first immutable arg slot (immutable arg offset 0x0); the mutant reads the second immutable arg (0x14) so when the first and second encoded immutable addresses differ the mutant returns a different owner — the test asserts owner() equals the first immutables-derived address encoded into the clone creation data and thus will fail for the mutant for some inputs.

For any clone deployed from C (reference), owner() returns the address encoded in the first immutable argument slot (the 0x0 offset), so owner() equals the first address in the creation data; the mutant reads the second immutable arg (0x14) and thus will return a different address whenever the first and second encoded addresses differ.

For any immutable args blob, the contract's collateral() getter always returns the ERC20 address encoded at the second immutable slot (offset 0x14); the mutant that reads offset 0x18 will sometimes return a different address (breaking this invariant).
